title: Embedding Core Business Policy Inside Database Queries
pattern: Core domain definitions and policies are embedded directly inside data queries, filters, or repository queries instead of being evaluated in pure memory-safe code.
why_bad: Violates persistence ignorance. Changes to business criteria (e.g., lowering the high-value threshold to $500) require modifying database queries, SQL views, or repository methods. Domain experts cannot easily verify or read code hidden in SQL queries.
detection: Complex filtering expressions (`WHERE` clauses with multiple business criteria) built directly in database layers or SQL string literals.
counterexample: Simple primary key lookups or simple status indexing. Marked `Context-dependent` if loading the entire record to evaluate in memory would cause severe performance problems.
source: Scott Wlaschin, *Domain Modeling made Functional* (2017), Chapter 10, "Persistence Ignorance", p. 211, 471.
